guide.title: Constrained minimal interventions
guide.summary: the cheapest change of declared inputs (weighted L1, Linf, squared L2, number changed) that attains a target or changes a predicate's membership, as an algebraic intervention with no causal claim: exact LPs and projections for linear targets under linear constraints, INV-001 roots for univariate polynomials with exact ties, exhaustive cost-ordered searches of finite grids listing every tie or proven bounds when incomplete (CPU and CUDA), and aggregates whose rows cross the predicate when a feature is shifted.

INV-002.cpu: Native minimal interventions: the change d of declared inputs (x = x0 + d) of minimal cost (weighted L1, Linf, squared L2 with rational weights, or the weighted number of changed inputs) such that the function attains a target f(x) op t (op =, !=, <, <=, >, >=) or, as a membership change, the complement of the predicate's value at x0 (decided exactly). Every result is labelled an algebraic intervention on the function as given (no causal model; causal semantics are refused as UNSUPPORTED). Linear targets (coefficients or first-slice expressions of degree <= 1, e.g. RESP-001 functions; n <= 16) under A x <= b, E x = e, boxes on x and d and the norm balls ||d||_1 <= r, ||d||_inf <= r: exact LPs (L1, Linf) and the exact projection QP (L2) by OPT-002's simplex and active-set methods, KKT-verified; L0 by supports in increasing weight (an exact feasibility LP each), every minimal support reported; strict targets on their closure with attainment decided by an LP over the optimal set (else UNATTAINED with the exact infimum); uniqueness by 2n LPs over the optimal set with a second optimal change when not unique. Univariate polynomial targets: the roots of f - t in the domain by INV-001 (exact rational roots or certified isolating intervals, refinable), the feasible set as points and open intervals decided by exact signs, the nearest feasible points on both sides compared exactly (a tie of irrational distances decided by a common root of (f - t)(x0 + y) and (f - t)(x0 - y)). Finite grids (1..8 coordinates, at most 2^24 points, any first-slice polynomial target with up to 15 polynomial constraints and linear rows): every condition as an integer polynomial in cleared numerators whose sign is decided from residues modulo verified primes (INV-001) and Garner's digits; integer cost tables over a common denominator; grid blocks pruned soundly by outward-rounded interval enclosures (FND-009); the remaining points ordered by (exact cost, grid index) and scanned in chunks; the minimum and every tie of the minimal cost listed; past the iteration budget INCOMPLETE with a proven lower bound (every cheaper point examined or pruned), the best found as upper bound and a resume rank; the output budget truncates the ties explicitly. Aggregates over the selected rows of an FND-004 scope: COUNT(*), COUNT(v), SUM(v), AVG(v) WHERE x + d op c (v may be x, then shifted too) with SQL NULL semantics, piecewise in d with exact breakpoints c - x_k from a state of sorted distinct values with prefix sums built once; every piece decided exactly so rows entering and leaving the predicate are part of the objective, never the frozen row set; staleness refused through the scope. Budgets (variables, degree, support, tensor, states, iterations, output, bytes) are checked before allocation.
INV-002.gpu: tr_mgpu_interv_grid: the batched exhaustive evaluation of a chunk of a grid plan's cost order. Launch 1: one work item per point evaluates every condition by its exact sign (residues modulo the verified primes, Garner's digits compared with (M - 1) / 2) and its integer cost, sets its bit of the feasibility bitmap by atomic OR and lowers the minimal feasible cost by atomic minimum; launch 2: one work item per point sets its tie bit (feasible and of the matched cost) by atomic OR. The results do not depend on thread order and equal the CPU's tr_interv_grid_eval bit for bit (the same inline per-point functions of math_interv.h); Grid.search(backend='cuda') runs every chunk of the exact search on it with the same answers. The plan, the order, the search loop, the LPs, the roots and the aggregates run on the CPU. Compiled with nvcc for sm_80 and tested in the emulation with scrambled thread order; not yet run on a device.
limitations: Answers are algebraic interventions on the function as given: no causal model, no claim about changing inputs in the world.
Linear targets must be linear in the changed inputs; polynomial targets in several inputs are searched only over explicit finite grids (at most 8 coordinates and 2^24 points).
Convex constraints are limited to linear rows, boxes and the L1 / Linf norm balls; general convex sets are not supported.
The L0 cost enumerates supports (2^n, budgeted) and the L1 / Linf uniqueness test costs 2n further exact LPs, which is slow at n = 16.
Aggregates shift one feature with one comparison predicate and support COUNT, SUM and AVG; changes at irrational roots are reported as isolating intervals.
The CUDA kernels have been compiled with nvcc and verified in the emulation only; no device run yet.
